intro: Lesson 7: Online exploitation and grooming: spotting and reporting. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

panels.title: What is grooming?
points: Can be for crime, money or abuse

panels.title: Warning signs
points: Asks to move to a private app

panels.title: Reporting
points: Tell a parent or the safeguarding lead

questions.q: Highlight each warning sign and name it.
questions.a: 1 flattery; 2 gifts and secrets; 3 turning them against parents (isolation); 4 move to a private app; 5 secrecy and isolation; 6 threats and control.

questions.q: What should the young person do now?
questions.a: Stop replying; do not pay or send anything; screenshot; block and report in the app; tell a parent or the TGA safeguarding lead; report to CEOP (ceop.police.uk).

keywords.def: building trust with a young person in order to exploit them
the National Crime Agency's child protection command, which takes reports online
controls over who sees and contacts you

questions.q: List three warning signs from the slides.
questions.a: Secrets, gifts, moving to a private app.

questions.q: Core: Chat analysis (pupil PDF, invented): highlight warning signs and write what the young person should do.
questions.a: Signs identified; stop, screenshot, block, tell, report.

questions.q: Extend: Check your own privacy settings on one app with a parent and record two changes.
Stretch: In the portal response box, explain why victims are never to blame. Start: 'Victims are never to blame because...'
questions.a: Victims are never to blame because groomers deliberately deceive and manipulate them.

questions.q: An online contact says 'Keep our chats secret from your parents'. This is...
questions.a: B) A warning sign of grooming. Isolation from trusted adults is a key grooming tactic.

questions.q: CEOP is... A) a game B) a place to report online child exploitation C) a social network
questions.a: B) a place to report online child exploitation
options: A place to report online exploitation

questions.q: Big question: kind, gifts, 'only I understand you': friendship or grooming?
questions.a: Possibly grooming: these are warning signs; tell a trusted adult.
